boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named UO destinations for studying, making, gathering, and connecting outside a standard campus-tour route.

cards.title: Erb Memorial Union
cards.subtitle: Campus hub for study, food, services, and student involvement
cards.notes: Use the union as a practical between-class base: meet a collaborator, find a study seat, use campus services, or check its event calendar.
cards.short_summary: A mixed-use campus hub built around student activities and everyday services.
cards.evidence_claim: UO identifies the EMU as its campus union and says it is the center for student activities and involvement, with spaces to meet, hang out, and study.
cards.access_notes: Located at 1395 University St.; building hours and holiday exceptions are posted by the EMU.

cards.title: O Lounge
cards.subtitle: Erb Memorial Union informal study space
cards.notes: Bring a classmate and plug in for an informal work session; the booths and interactive screens suit short group check-ins between commitments.
cards.short_summary: An EMU lounge configured for informal classmate study groups.
cards.evidence_claim: The EMU describes the O Lounge as having booths and interactive TV screens for classmates to plug in devices for informal study groups.
cards.access_notes: Inside the EMU; confirm building access and any event-related restrictions before visiting.

cards.title: Craft Center
cards.subtitle: Creative studios in the Erb Memorial Union
cards.notes: Check workshop and orientation registration before planning a project, then choose a studio aligned with the material or process you want to try.
cards.short_summary: A campus studio center spanning ceramics, wood, glass, photo, print, fiber, and more.
cards.evidence_claim: The Craft Center says its EMU studios include darkroom photography, woodworking, glassworking, paper arts, printmaking, fiber arts, jewelry, painting, drawing, and ceramics.
cards.access_notes: Located in the EMU; workshop and studio participation may require registration or an orientation.

cards.title: Mills International Center
cards.subtitle: EMU mezzanine resource center for intercultural connection
cards.notes: Drop in for a language circle or program, or use the space to meet people across cultures; its services welcome international and U.S. students.
cards.short_summary: A student resource center focused on belonging and cross-cultural learning.
cards.evidence_claim: Mills International Center says it is a space for international and U.S. UO students to interact, learn, build community, and develop cross-cultural understanding.
cards.access_notes: EMU mezzanine, Room 102; the center publishes separate summer and academic-year hours.

cards.title: Knight Library
cards.subtitle: UO’s largest library on the west side of campus
cards.notes: Choose a quiet area for individual work or reserve a room when your project needs conversation, shared screens, or a dedicated study block.
cards.short_summary: The main campus library with quiet areas, collections, and reservable study rooms.
cards.evidence_claim: Knight Library provides reservable rooms for individual and collaborative study, along with teaching and learning support services.
cards.access_notes: 1501 Kincaid St.; library hours and room-reservation rules are published by UO Libraries.

cards.title: Douglass Room
cards.subtitle: Knight Library’s music and audio resource hub
cards.notes: Use the listening stations or creative workstations when coursework calls for sound; confirm recording-studio availability and any needed reservations first.
cards.short_summary: A third-floor library space for music research, listening, and audio production.
cards.evidence_claim: UO Libraries describes the Douglass Room as a third-floor Knight Library hub with listening stations, creative workstations, an audio collection, and recording studios.
cards.access_notes: Located on the third floor of Knight Library; check library hours and studio access requirements.

cards.title: DREAM Lab
cards.subtitle: Knight Library digital research and media workspace
cards.notes: Plan a collaborative digital project here and use a walk-in or reservable option as appropriate; check the room listing before bringing a group.
cards.short_summary: A library lab supporting digital research, education, and media work.
cards.evidence_claim: UO Libraries states that the DREAM Lab has reservable and walk-in spaces for collaborative digital research, education, and media initiatives.
cards.access_notes: In Knight Library; some spaces are reservable while others are walk-in.

cards.title: Many Nations Longhouse
cards.subtitle: Native student and community gathering place
cards.notes: Attend only appropriately open programs or invitations, and treat the longhouse as a cultural and community space rather than a casual event venue.
cards.short_summary: A longhouse that supports Native student organizations, study, and community gatherings.
cards.evidence_claim: UO says the Many Nations Longhouse is used for personal, cultural, social, and academic events and has long served Native students as a place to study and socialize.
cards.source_title: Native Indigenous Students at the UO
cards.access_notes: Use is connected to cultural, academic, and community events; follow host and program access guidance.

cards.title: Lyllye Reynolds-Parker Black Cultural Center
cards.subtitle: Academic, cultural, and social home for Black students
cards.notes: Look for center programming or request a reservable room for an eligible gathering that supports the BCC’s mission and its student community.
cards.short_summary: A campus cultural center supporting Black students’ community and academic life.
cards.evidence_claim: UO describes the Lyllye Reynolds-Parker Black Cultural Center as an academic, cultural, and social home for Black students and the community.
cards.access_notes: Reservable venues are for UO students, faculty, staff, and partners when gatherings support the BCC mission.

cards.entity_name: Museum of Natural and Cultural History
cards.title: Museum of Natural and Cultural History
cards.subtitle: UO campus museum on East 15th Avenue
cards.notes: Build in time for the current exhibits, and bring your UO ID for student admission; use the museum’s directions page to plan bicycle, transit, or parking access.
cards.short_summary: A campus museum presenting Oregon’s natural and cultural history through exhibits.
cards.evidence_claim: The Museum of Natural and Cultural History states that it is on the University of Oregon campus and that UO students are admitted free with ID.
cards.access_notes: 1680 East 15th Avenue; open Wednesday–Sunday, with Thursday hours extending to 8 p.m.; UO student ID is required for free admission.
